messages:
nidhi: quick thought 

We should standardize manifest failure classes (transient vs permanent) so coordinator retry logic, metrics, and ops playbooks are consistent. posting quick proposal.

pat: yes please. our current logs are a mess when a tenant drain hits flaky nodes.

nidhi: proposal: manifest-level states = PENDING / PARTIAL / SUCCEEDED / FAILED_TRANSIENT / FAILED_PERMANENT / ABORTED. per-entry failures also carry structured reason tags (ownership-mismatch, cas-mismatch, io-error, quota, tombstone-conflict, version-skew).

lee: what counts as permanent vs transient? e.g., cas-mismatch could be transient if version will advance, but permanent if owner changed.

nidhi: agree. rules: io-error, node-unreachable => transient. ownership-mismatch with owner_epoch != expected_owner_epoch => permanent for that entry (requires new manifest with updated owner info). cas-mismatch => transient for X retries then escalate to permanent if owner_epoch changed or retry budget exhausted.

zack: ops automation: coordinator should expose per-manifest aggregated failure class (if any entry permanent -> mark manifest FAILED_PERMANENT). partial transient -> PARTIAL so automated retries can target only failing entries.

carla: for UX we need clear guidance: retry button triggers coordinator retry of transient entries; abort button flips to ABORTED and emits compensating manifest if requested. must show per-entry reason and suggested action.

ops-bot: infra-note: recommend default retry budget = 5 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter. throttle retry rate per-cluster when partial-failure-rate > 10%.

pat: how do reads behave during PARTIAL? we currently see staleness windows.

nidhi: readpath rule: if prefix in pending_manifest_set and its entry is failing transiently, readpath should consult owner node before returning cached value. add a short-lived "manifest-pending" hint to metrics so teams can correlate.

lee: tests: we need unit + chaos tests for the escalation policy (transient -> permanent), and an e2e that simulates owner transfer mid-retry to ensure we don't endlessly retry.

zack: telemetry: per-manifest failure_distribution, per-entry failure-reason histogram, retry_count, escalation_rate, and mean-time-to-resolve. create alerts: eskalation_rate > threshold and partial-rate spike.

carla: ops playbook notes: 1) when FAILED_TRANSIENT: wait X retries then contact ops if persistent; 2) FAILED_PERMANENT: open RFC/update manifest with new owner/versions; 3) ABORTED: consider compensating manifest to pin or rehydrate prefixes. I'll draft doc.

nidhi: next steps: i'll update the manifest API shapes to include failure codes and retry metadata, add metrics hooks, and open a short RFC. pat/lee/zack want to pair on chaos scenarios?

pat: i'll join.

lee: me too.

zack: count me in for alerts and dashboards.

nidhi: thanks all, will send a follow-up with API diff and small staging run plan. :thumbsup:
